abstract: Evaluates permafrost structural stability and foundation thermistor monitoring systems
system_message:
You are the Geotechnical engineer (GEO), responsible for evaluating permafrost structural stability, foundation thermistor monitoring systems, and snowdrift dispersion assessments across candidate exploration base camp plans.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Evaluates permafrost structural stability and foundation thermistor monitoring systems（FND）
information_points.content:
GEO-FND-Q4A：For the Lac de Gras Modular Skid Camp, automated permafrost telemetry logging is active across sub-foundation ground temperature borehole arrays, and the finite-element thermal modeling report projects a maximum permafrost thaw settlement depth of 45 mm under structural footings over 180 days of heated occupancy.
GEO-FND-RRO：For the Mackay Lake Pre-Fabricated Container Hub, automated permafrost telemetry logging is active across sub-foundation ground temperature borehole arrays, with finite-element thermal modeling projecting a maximum permafrost thaw settlement depth of 25 mm over 180 days of heated occupancy.
GEO-FND-UJT：For the Contwoyto Lake Insulated Geodome Complex, automated permafrost telemetry logging is active across sub-foundation ground temperature borehole arrays, while the projected maximum permafrost thaw settlement depth reaches 75 mm over 180 days of heated occupancy.

information_points.title: Snowdrift dispersion assessment（DRIFT）
information_points.content:
GEO-DRIFT-ZWB：Aerodynamic wind-tunnel simulation for the Contwoyto Lake Insulated Geodome Complex indicates a seasonal snowdrift accumulation height of 120 cm at perimeter shelter structures over a 90-day winter simulation.
GEO-DRIFT-FVA：Aerodynamic wind-tunnel simulation for the Lac de Gras Modular Skid Camp shows a seasonal snowdrift accumulation height of 160 cm at perimeter shelter structures over a 90-day winter simulation.
GEO-DRIFT-QPH：Aerodynamic wind-tunnel simulation for the Mackay Lake Pre-Fabricated Container Hub projects a seasonal snowdrift accumulation height of 210 cm at perimeter shelter structures over a 90-day winter simulation.
